title: Killed literals vanish under the induced assignment
statement: Fix $n$ and let $l$ be a literal on $n$ variables, with underlying variable $v \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$ and polarity flag $b \in \{\text{false}, \text{true}\}$ (with $b = \text{true}$ marking a negated literal). Let $\rho$ be a restriction on $n$ variables that kills $l$, meaning $\rho$ fixes $v$ to the value $b$. Then for every assignment $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \{\text{false}, \text{true}\}$, the literal $l$ evaluates to false at the extension of $x$ along $\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: l is a literal on n variables with variable v and polarity b
ρ is a restriction that kills l, i.e. ρ(v) = b
replaced:
If a literal $l$ is killed by $\rho$, then for every $x$ it evaluates to false on the
extended point: $l.\mathrm{eval}(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x) = \mathrm{false}$.
